title: Changing the schema of a live table without an outage

videos.script: Adding a column to a table takes a few milliseconds. And it can still take a website down. {{column}} Here is how. A report opens a transaction, reads the table, and stays open. Your ALTER TABLE arrives and needs the table to itself, so it waits. {{wait}} That part you expect. What you do not expect is the next query, an ordinary page view. It queues behind your ALTER. So does the one after it, and the hundred after that. {{queue}} Nothing is happening, and nobody is being served. This lesson starts by building that queue on purpose, in three terminals, and watching it in pg_stat_activity. {{watch}} Then the habit that defuses it: a lock timeout, and a retry. {{timeout}} Then the changes themselves. Some only edit the catalogue and are instant at any size. Others rewrite every row while the table is closed. You will measure both on a million rows. {{measure}} And for the expensive ones, a way round: add the new column beside the old one, fill it in batches, switch, and drop the old one. Each step short, and none of them an outage. {{expand}}
